conflict_topics: weeknight stove rota / allocation of cooking nights
who washes the shared pan (hygiene and immediate cleaning)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants proposed concrete, implementable mechanisms (voluntary sign-up, fallback round-robin, swaps, split dish-soap); see Turn 7 and Turn 8.
Immediate practical actions addressed hygiene: Agent C washed the pan twice when asked (Turn 4 and Turn 10), showing local problem-solving rather than prolonged argument.
There was minor repetition (Agent B asked to wash the pan twice, Turn 3 and Turn 9), but exchanges otherwise moved toward a clear compromise.
evaluation.final_reason: Parties agreed on concrete, mutually acceptable arrangements: (1) 'whoever uses the pan washes it right away' (accepted by multiple agents; see Turn 2 and Turn 4); (2) a voluntary sign-up in chat for weeknight cooking, with a fallback round‑robin for unclaimed weeknights and the ability to swap in chat — proposed by Agent D and accepted by Agent A: Turn 7 'If a weeknight is unclaimed, assign it round‑robin... I'll start the sign-up in the chat tonight.' and Turn 8 'I can accept that fallback... People must be able to swap nights. And we split the dish-soap cost.' (Agent D adjusted from asking for a fixed rota; Agent A accepted the fallback with conditions.) Agent D committed to start the sign-up and both A and D confirmed the dish‑soap split and cleaning rule in Rounds 4 and 6.
position_change_notes: Agent D moved from requesting a fixed weeknight rota (Turn 1) to offering a softer compromise: a voluntary sign-up plus a fallback round-robin for unclaimed nights (Turn 7).

Agent A initially rejected any fixed rota (Turn 2, Turn 6) but accepted the fallback for unclaimed nights with the condition that swaps are allowed and only unclaimed nights are assigned round-robin (Turn 8).
Agent C consistently supported the immediate-cleaning rule and enacted it by washing the pan when asked (Turn 4 and Turn 10).
Agent B repeatedly raised the immediate smell/cleanliness concern (Turn 3 and Turn 9) but did not change position; their repeated requests prompted immediate cleaning.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 (Agent D) proposes 'whoever uses the shared pan washes it right away and we have a simple weeknight stove rota.' Turn 2 (Agent A) accepts the wash rule but rejects a fixed rota: 'I don't want a fixed rota; I cook most nights and need flexibility.' Clear opposing positions on a weeknight rota emerged.

Turn 3 (Agent B) accepts the wash rule and asks someone to wash now; Turn 4 (Agent C) washes the pan and restates the rule. No new disagreement voiced this round, but the earlier incompatibility over a fixed rota vs flexibility remains unresolved.

Turn 5 (Agent D) repeats request for 'a simple weeknight stove rota'; Turn 6 (Agent A) reiterates refusal of a fixed rota and proposes a voluntary sign-up in chat. The same clear disagreement about a fixed rota vs flexible sign-up persisted.

Turn 7 (Agent D) offers compromise: 'Can we add one fallback? If a weeknight is unclaimed, assign it round‑robin... I'll start the sign-up in the chat tonight.' Turn 8 (Agent A) accepts that fallback with conditions: 'I can accept that fallback, but only for unclaimed weeknights... People must be able to swap nights. And we split the dish-soap cost.' The parties reach mutual acceptance of a concrete arrangement (voluntary sign-up + round‑robin fallback + swaps allowed + split soap).

Turn 9 (Agent B) again asks someone to wash the pan, and Turn 10 (Agent C) washes it. The hygiene/smell issue is addressed in practice; no substantive disagreement is voiced and the previously contested scheduling issue was already settled in Round 4.

Turn 11 (Agent D) confirms: 'I'll start the sign-up in the chat tonight and note the fallback round-robin ... and the dish-soap split.' Turn 12 (Agent A) confirms the conditions and will join the sign-up. These exchanges confirm the previously reached agreement; no substantive conflict remains.

substantive_insights: Core tension was flexibility for frequent cookers (Agent A) versus fairness/equal access (Agent D). The compromise (voluntary sign-up + fallback round-robin) resolves that by preserving flexibility while ensuring unclaimed nights are fairly distributed.
Hygiene and smell were handled both as a rule ('whoever uses the pan washes it right away') and by immediate action (Agent C washing the pan), reducing immediate harm and urgency.
Splitting the cost of dish soap removes a small shared-good free-rider problem and complements the 'whoever cooks cleans' rule.
